measurements.pitch: Flag on, tone 440 Hz, zero-crossing frequency 440.00 Hz within 0.00 cents and DFT peak 440 at 2, 1/2, 3/2, 3/4, 4, 1/4, 5, 8, 16, 1/8, 1/16; exact lengths ceil(window / speed); energy at the moved pitch below 0.00004 of the tone. Flag off, same measure: the moved pitch (880, 220, 660, 330, 1760, 110, 2200, 3520, 7040, 55, 27.5 Hz).
measurements.burst: 0.5 s tone at 1 s of a 3 s window: 2x lands at samples 23808..36096 against 24000..36000; 1/2 at 96000..144128 against 96000..144000.
measurements.reverse: Rising sweep 300..600 Hz at -2: flag on falls 540.0 -> 359.9 Hz, forward at 2x rises 360.1 -> 540.1 Hz, flag off falls 1080 -> 720 Hz.
measurements.stereo: 330 Hz left and 660 Hz right at 3/2: 330.00 and 660.00 Hz.
measurements.stretch_cost: 10 s stereo source at 2x in a debug build, mix built and rendered: flag on 1.20 s, flag off 2.49 s. The stretch costs less than the resampler it replaces, so it adds no load to session build. Not a release-build figure.
measurements.flow_budget: 920 x 920 refused frame_interpolation_unavailable, Composite(BudgetExceeded), after 4.1 s in a debug build: the two frames are rendered before Pigment's admission refuses.

notes.spec_basis: Master Spec v02.229 14-studio-creative-suite.md STU-VID-031: `frame_sampling` "Nearest source frame"; `frame_blending` "Weighted blend of the two neighbouring source frames"; `optical_flow` "MUST be marked as an estimation in any diagnostic that compares it to a source frame"; "`Maintain audio pitch` is an independent boolean".

brief_answers.floor_against_nearest: They disagree at every non-unit speed with a position nearer the later frame: 3/4 at timeline frame 1 is source 0.75; clip_source_at gave tick 0.75 F, which the decoder reads as frame 0; the spec's nearest is frame 1. Also reverse: clip_source_at gave source_out at the head, the tick after the window, frame_unavailable at the end of a source. The spec wins at non-unit speeds. clip_source_at itself is unchanged: it is the tick mapping and other paths read it; frame_layers no longer takes its frame from it there.
brief_answers.stretch_and_the_block_mix: stretch serves the mix with no Score change. The block-based stream builds a whole clip into a TrackSpec when a group's session is built; blocks read that buffer. So the clip goes through StreamingStretch once at build. StreamingStretch rather than time_stretch: time_stretch refuses output above 2^25 samples (11.6 min at 48 kHz) and would refuse the whole mix over one long clip; with transients off StreamingStretch is bit-identical to it (score test streaming_without_transients_is_bit_identical_to_the_offline_stretch).
brief_answers.reverse_with_the_flag: The window plays backward with each tone at its own pitch and the speed's duration: reversed, then stretched. At -1 the flag changes nothing: the exact reverse keeps the pitch. UNVERIFIED (D5).
brief_answers.drop_policy_when_pixel_motion_misses_the: The render is synchronous with no deadline and is never abandoned or replaced by a mix. Then the scheduler answers as for any late frame: DropLate presents the due frame and counts the skipped ones (shown 0, 3, 6, 9, dropped 6 with each render taking 3 frames); PresentEveryFrame presents each frame in order and lag grows (shown 0, 1, 2, 3, dropped 0, lag 6 frames). The caller's thread is blocked for the render. Test a_late_estimate_follows_the_existing_drop_policy, which advances a headless clock between refreshes: no real slow render was timed.
brief_answers.wall_clock_tests: The two 400 ms tests are in the harness crate, not harness-view: tests/audio_import.rs:360 and tests/viewer_audio.rs:225. See tests.wall_clock_watch.

declared_readings: UNVERIFIED (D5): unit speed forward with frame_sampling keeps the frame holding its tick, which off the source grid can differ from the nearest frame. The brief's rule: unit-speed output must not change. The spec's nearest applies at every other speed; frame_blending and optical_flow at unit speed blend off the grid.
UNVERIFIED (D5): a source whose grid no port states reads on its sequence's frame grid; a nested sequence on its own rate.

UNVERIFIED (D5): in a transition handle the position law runs past the window, bounded by a known source length or, unknown, by the window; inside the clip only frames of the window are named, so the last source frame of a window does not blend with the frame after it.
A share of 0 needs one frame and no blend, whatever the method; an optical_flow clip keeps its mark there, though the pixels are the source frame: the spec's duty stays on the safe side.
A frame hold is one real source frame: Held, no mark, whatever the method.

Each frame is fitted to the monitor raster before the blend, so pixel_motion's budget is charged at the raster, not the source: a large source on a small monitor can estimate. Limit: BlendLimits::DEFAULT 2e10 visits at FlowParams::DEFAULT, 826719 pixels, so by that arithmetic a 1920 x 1080 raster is refused (the refusal was run at 920 x 920 only).

UNVERIFIED (D5): the estimator is Pigment's Horn-Schunck with no occlusion reasoning. Measured on a 4-wide bar moving 6: brightest columns in the right place, faint residue at the source positions; on a bar crossing a post it overdraws the post. The artefact the spec names; the frame carries the mark.
UNVERIFIED (D5): speeds past the vocoder's 1/4..4 take two passes. Premiere's range for Maintain Audio Pitch is not known here.

Transients off in the stretch: channels are stretched separately, and an onset detected on one only would shift it against the other. Percussive material smears more than it would with transients on; not measured.
